method: Cross-check of built-in default factors and tabulated engine constants against openly accessible documents. The criteria of the suite manifest were grouped by underlying constant and ranked (partial safety factors and utilisation limits first, then model coefficients and engine tables). For each group an open document was downloaded and its text read; an entry is marked "matches" or "differs" only where the value was read in the opened document and the quote is taken from its text. Sources are free editions of primary standards (mainly DNV documents, several of them earlier editions retrieved from the publisher's former open archive via the Internet Archive), official manuals, technical reports, and secondary sources that reproduce a clause of a standard that is not itself open; the kind is stated per entry. "edition-dependent" means the editions read or cited give different values, both of which are stated; "not-found" means no open text containing the value could be read and names where it should be confirmed. Quotes are copied from the text layer of the documents, so spacing, decimal commas and transliterated symbols follow that layer; equations and tables stored as images could not be read and are flagged in the notes. Many entries were read in an edition older than the one the module cites. This is a plausibility cross-check, not a substitute for checking each factor against the governing edition named in a project's design basis.
